title: Bank Reconciliation
description: Reconcile the company's cash records with the bank statement.
html:
Why do bank and book balances differ?

The cash balance in a company's accounting records may differ from the balance shown on its bank statement.

A bank reconciliation explains those differences.

Bank-side adjustments

Deposits in transit

Deposits recorded by the company that have not yet appeared on the bank statement.

These are generally added to the bank balance.

Outstanding checks

Checks recorded by the company that have not yet cleared the bank.

These are generally subtracted from the bank balance.

Book-side adjustments

Some items appear on the bank statement before the company records them.

  • Bank service charges
  • NSF customer checks
  • Interest earned
  • Automatic collections or payments

Example

Bank statement balance $20,000
Add: Deposit in transit $3,000
Less: Outstanding checks ($2,000)
Adjusted bank balance $21,000

Important

Deposits in transit and outstanding checks usually do not require new journal entries because the company has already recorded them.

Book-side items such as bank fees or NSF checks generally do require journal entries.

quiz.prompt: A company has a $15,000 bank balance, a $2,000 deposit in transit and $1,500 of outstanding checks. What is the adjusted bank balance?

objectives: Explain bank reconciliation and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
